transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is this thing I’ve been noticing at work and on calls. It’s not, like, dramatic, but during sprint planning meetings or even mortgage calls—times I know I should just stay seated and focus—I keep getting up. I’ll suddenly decide I need water, or I’ll go check something in another room.

I know that probably sounds small, but it’s happening enough that I’m wondering if it’s something I should get help understanding.
Do you often feel restless or find it hard to stay seated, even when you know you should?

Yes… I mean, not constantly, but enough that I’ve noticed it. Like during sprint planning meetings or those mortgage calls where I know I’m supposed to just sit there and pay attention, I’ll suddenly get up for water or decide I need to check something in another room.

It feels a little silly saying it out loud, because it’s not like I’m trying to be disruptive or anything. I just… have a hard time staying put sometimes, even when I know I should.
Do you ever feel an inner sense of restlessness, like you can't relax or you feel driven to move, even when you’re not particularly anxious or upset?

Yeah… I think so. I wouldn’t say I’m upset when it happens, necessarily. It’s more like… even if I look calm sitting there, inside there’s this pressure, like I need to move or switch to something else or just do something with my hands.

It’s not unbearable all the time, but sometimes it feels like if I don’t do something, I’m going to crawl out of my skin a little. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks, especially ones that require sustained attention, like paperwork or long meetings?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can usually start okay, like reviewing a pull request or reading through mortgage documents, and I have good intentions. But then after a few minutes I’ll realize I’m just kind of staring at the same section and my mind is off thinking about five totally unrelated things.

It’s not like I never get anything done, so I don’t want to overstate it, but it does happen enough that it feels… frustrating. Does that count as what you mean?
Do you often find yourself interrupting others during conversations or acting on impulse without thinking it through?

A little, yeah. I don’t think I’m constantly interrupting people, or at least I hope I’m not… but at work I do catch myself jumping in before someone’s finished explaining a bug or asking a question.

Sometimes I’m already answering and then I realize, oh, I guessed wrong about where they were going with that. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I usually try to backtrack or say sorry, but it does happen. Is that the kind of impulse thing you mean?
Do you notice these difficulties with restlessness, focus, or impulsivity in other settings, like at home, in social situations, or during downtime, or do they only seem to happen at work?

It’s not only work, no. I mean, work is where it’s most obvious because there are deadlines and other people are depending on me, but… it does show up at home too.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I am trying really hard to stay on top of things. But there’s been more friction lately. People have to follow up with me more than they used to, and I feel bad about that. Like for planning things or keeping track of what needs to happen, I worry I’m becoming the unreliable one, even though that’s really not what I want.

Does that answer what you’re asking?

Looking back, were you aware of these kinds of difficulties with restlessness, staying focused, or acting impulsively when you were a child, or do they seem to have developed more recently in adulthood?

I think it goes back pretty far, yeah. I don’t know that I thought of it as a “problem” then, exactly, but I do remember in elementary school teachers moving my desk or reminding me to stay seated.

I was kind of the kid who would pop up a lot, or talk before I was called on. And I’d rush through assignments even when I understood the work, which… I guess maybe looked careless. I don’t want to blame everything on that, but it wasn’t only something that started recently. Does that help?

Do you also notice these behaviors—like feeling restless, acting impulsively, or having trouble staying focused—in other situations, like when you’re out in public, driving, or spending time with friends?

Yeah… I mean, I think it shows up outside of work too, though maybe not as obviously. I don’t want to overstate it.

The main thing is it’s started causing some friction, both at work and at home. People have to remind me or follow up with me more than they used to, especially around planning things or keeping track of tasks. And I really am trying, so it feels bad when I worry I’m becoming the unreliable one.

I’m not sure if that’s exactly what you mean by in public or with friends, but it’s not just isolated to one place.
Can you think of specific examples of when you’ve felt restless, had trouble focusing, or acted impulsively at home, with friends, or in other non-work situations?

Yeah, I can think of a few. I don’t know if this is the kind of example you mean, but even with something normal at home, like reading mortgage documents or reviewing a pull request outside of a meeting, I’ll start with good intentions and really plan to focus.

Then a few minutes later I realize I’ve been staring at the same paragraph or section and I’m not actually taking it in. My mind is off on, like, five unrelated things. It’s not that I don’t care or that I’m trying to avoid it… I just sort of lose the thread and have to bring myself back.

It’s not every single time, but it happens enough that I notice it. Does that make sense?
Can you recall times when you’ve felt restless or had trouble staying still or focused in situations like being in a car, waiting in line, or trying to relax during downtime?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not always obvious, because I can usually keep myself sitting there and look normal, I guess.

But inside I sometimes feel this kind of pressure, like I need to move or switch tasks or do something with my hands. Like if I’m supposed to just relax, or I’m stuck waiting, I can get this uncomfortable feeling where sitting still feels harder than it should. Not dramatic, exactly, but almost like I’m going to crawl out of my skin if I don’t do something.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of restlessness you mean.
